name: Moraima de Córdoba
vampire_desc: The wife of the Moorish King of Grenada, when the area was taken by the Christians in 1236, Moraima was taken as hostage to Cordoba and trapped in the palace, stripped of her titles, and navigating a new life as a Morisca, forced to convert to Christianity. Her father was a royal physician and she used this knowledge to leverage herself into some autonomy, proving medical care for the destitute in Cordoba.

marks.description: Twining, vine-like markings that blaze blood red on the skin of the hands, arms and neck when the curse of the dead begins to grasp the soul, awakening the predatorial instincts of Neshama K’vura
marks.concealment: Heavy robes that cover the skin and calf skin gloves over the hands.

experiences: The wife of the Moorish King of Grenada, when the area was taken by the Christians in 1236, Moraima was taken as hostage to Cordoba and trapped in the palace, stripped of her titles, and navigating a new life as a Morisca, forced to convert to Christianity. Her father was a royal physician and she used this knowledge to leverage herself into some autonomy, proving medical care for the destitute in Cordoba.

The day her father gave her the tool roll of instruments when he deemed she was capable of treating basic ailments and injuries independently. That afternoon she went down to the kitchens of the palace and did just that,

Giving Paloma La Partera two of the precious gold coins that had been stitched into her cotte by her loyal childhood nursemaid when she left her father’s home to marry. The coins were used to by vital ingredients to treat the group of beaten women of ill repute whose bruises had been obtained during a illicit masquerade party held by one of the most respected and cruel Dukes of Cordoba.

On the occasion of her child’s second birthday, when he had survived the perilous early years of childhood, her husband gifted her a filigree locket, delicate and beautiful with a motif of an exotic flower. Within was a tiny etching of this precious child and a small compartment.

Though vampires are often turned down darkened alleyways, Moses Maimonides rejects such prosaic, tawdry impulses, instead turning his descendants in a sacrosanct ritual of legacy. Beaten to the point of near death after saving the life of the mistress of a wealthy Count, was taken by Maimon ben Yosef to the surgery of  Moses Maimonides in hopes of eternal resurrection for his compassionate friend, colleague and sometime lover. After some questioning and soul searching, Maimonides agreed to the transformation, laying her out on the altar and saying prayers over her before exchanging blood and laying her to rest, ready to reawaken as one of the Neshama K’vur

skills.name: The Adab: the ability to give comfort and dignity to others.

resources.name: A filigree locket
resources.description: A delicate construction of gold with the motif of an exotic flower. Within is a small chamber where tiny items can be hidden.

resources.name: Wicker basket
resources.description: Inside is a leather wrap of instruments - scalpel, forceps, needle and sutures, opium, camphor, honey, distilled alcohol.

resources.name: Cotte.
resources.description: a tightly-laced, stiffened under-bodice, with gold coins quilted between the inner layers of canvas

characters.name: Nafi al-Garnati
characters.description: Her father, respected Nabib to the royal court. Raised his daughter at his right hand, passing on the secrets of medicine and teaching principles of pragmatism and compassion.

characters.name: Ahmed ibn Malik al-Boabdil al-Garnati
characters.description: Her son. Taken alongside his mother at the age of 3 and raised in the Christian court and baptised. They were kept separated, with him being raised as a squire, but fell ill. She was not allowed to tend him and he died of dysentery aged 9.

characters.name: Maimon ben Yosef
characters.description: A Sephardic Jewish Boticario in the Suq al-Attarin. She has a long standing professional and occasional intimate relationship as he supplies her with the ingredients she uses to craft medicine. A widower.

characters.name: Paloma "La Partera"
characters.description: Castilian midwife: rough-tongued, practical, and carries the keys to the slum of Cordoba. She sees all and knows all, delivering babies from the most destitute of working girls to the secret mistresses of wealthy knights.

characters.name: Moses Maimonides,  רוֹפֵא הָעוֹלָם
characters.description: Name meaning ‘Rofeh Ha'Olam’ or ‘Eternal Healer’. Having dedicated his life to healing, in the latter years Maimonides turned his study to extending life, stumbling into the grey world of the afterlife and, more importantly, the undead. He committed Pidyon Nefesh b’Dam, The Ransom of the Soul in Blood, to pursue the path of healing for his people, making himself Neshama K’vura (The Buried Soul). Having staged his death in 1203, he cultivated a network of trusted healers to continue his life’s work, on occasion deigning to add another to his own damned fate when all other avenues have been exhausted.
